acceptance.given: An aggregate executes with an applicable output bound.

oracle.expected: Recorded aggregate output is at or below the applicable bound during runtime execution.
forbidden: Any aggregate exceeds its output bound.
oracle.observable: Runtime aggregate execution record containing output amount and applicable bound.

acceptance.then: The aggregate execution record demonstrates bounded output and a deterministic terminal state.
acceptance.when: During runtime verification, execute each aggregate and inspect its recorded output against the applicable bound.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an aggregate execution whose output exceeds its bound or fails to reach a deterministic terminal observation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce bounded aggregate output and deterministic terminal observation during runtime execution.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing aggregate invocation and result schema; rollback removes only bound enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate executing -> bounded output recorded -> deterministic terminal state
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every aggregate execution records output at or below its applicable bound and a deterministic terminal status; budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: A reference semantic verdict and pinned evaluation inputs are available for a fresh checkout.

oracle.expected: The fresh-checkout semantic verdict equals the reference semantic verdict.
forbidden: The fresh-checkout semantic verdict differs from the reference verdict.
The result cannot be reproduced from the pinned inputs.
oracle.observable: Fresh-checkout replay result containing semantic verdict and comparison to the reference verdict.

acceptance.then: The replay report records the same semantic verdict as the reference run.
acceptance.when: Execute the evaluation in a fresh checkout with pinned inputs, rebuilding the original binding identity before replay, then compare its semantic verdict with the reference verdict.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a fresh-checkout replay with pinned inputs that deterministically produces a semantic verdict different from the reference.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Rebuild the original binding identity before replay and compare the fresh-checkout semantic verdict with the reference verdict using pinned inputs; reject changed identity.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep replay input and result formats backward compatible; rollback removes only fresh-checkout verdict comparison.

slice_hint.state_transition: reference verdict + pinned inputs -> original binding identity rebuilt -> same-identity fresh-checkout replay -> verdict comparison
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Fresh-checkout execution reproduces the reference semantic verdict from pinned inputs after original-binding reconstruction and same-identity replay; identity mismatch is rejected.

acceptance.given: Every applicable Consumer has a defined Prior Route identity before the operation sequence.

oracle.expected: After enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through real call surfaces, the Consumer Route identity matches the Prior Route identity.
forbidden: The resulting Route identity differs from the Prior Route identity.
Prior Route identity restoration is omitted.
oracle.observable: Real-call-surface trace and final Consumer Route identity compared with the captured Prior Route identity.

acceptance.then: The Consumer's final Route identity equals its captured Prior Route identity.
acceptance.when: Execute enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through each Consumer's real call surface, then inspect the final Route identity.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a Consumer sequence where the final Route identity differs from the captured Prior Route identity or restoration is skipped.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Exercise the complete enable/disable/rollback/re-enable sequence through real call surfaces and assert restoration of the Prior Route identity.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve Consumer route state representation and existing call-surface compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Prior Route identity -> enable -> disable -> behavioral rollback -> re-enable -> restored Prior Route identity
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: For every applicable Consumer, the final Route identity equals the Prior Route identity after all four operations through real call surfaces.

acceptance.given: The evaluation-seed records are available for assembly or checking.

oracle.expected: Each of the three named evaluation seeds has exactly one record with required provenance and classification fields.
forbidden: Any named evaluation seed is missing.
Any named evaluation seed occurs more than once.
oracle.observable: Manifest artifact containing the three named seed identifiers and per-seed occurrence counts.

acceptance.then: The manifest contains exactly one occurrence for each named evaluation seed and preserves required provenance metadata.
acceptance.when: Run manifest validation and inspect the emitted manifest artifact for duplicate or missing named seed entries.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a manifest containing a missing or duplicate named evaluation-seed record, or lacking required provenance fields.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate exactly-once occurrence, provenance, applicability, missing labels, counterexample or explicit absence, and approved non-baseline classification for all three named seeds.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Maintain backward-compatible manifest fields while enforcing exactly-once seed membership and required provenance.

slice_hint.state_transition: seed records assembled -> manifest validation -> exactly-once named seed set
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation passes only when each named evaluation seed appears exactly once with required provenance and classification fields.
